identification.summary: TaskMasters is a cyber-espionage cluster reported by Positive Technologies in May 2019, named for its lateral-movement/persistence method of creating tasks in the Windows Task Scheduler [S2]. Positive Technologies reporting says it has been active for at least nine years (since about 2010) and compromised more than 30 organizations, 24 of them in Russia [S3]. Group-IB later linked the BlueTraveller (RemShell) malware family, which it associates with TaskMasters, to the Webdav-O Trojan used against Russian federal executive bodies in 2020 [S4].
identification.firstObserved: Reported as active for at least nine years as of the May 2019 Positive Technologies report [S3].
identification.notes: Kaspersky is reported to track the same cluster as BlueTraveler/BlueTraveller [S3]; I did not open a Kaspersky primary source, so treat the equivalence as secondary reporting. Group-IB could not say whether TA428 and TaskMasters are separate participants or units of one group, so the two clusters are not merged here [S4].

attribution.confidence: Positive Technologies' attribution to a Chinese-speaking/Asian origin is tentative per press coverage: ASPXSpy2014 web-shell code on GitHub references Chinese developers, but the sample found in the attacks referenced google.ru, and one log showed a switch to a residential Chinese IP while most requests came from Eastern European hosting and print-house IPs [S3]. Group-IB stated it could not confirm the identity of the 2020 attackers [S4].
attribution.basis: Tool and code indicators reported via secondary coverage of the PT report [S3]; Group-IB code and command-set overlap between Webdav-O and BlueTraveller [S4]. No source gathered names a state sponsor or government agency.

objectives: Theft of confidential information from victim organizations [S3]. Specific tasking or beneficiary is not stated in the sources gathered.

sectors: Government (federal executive bodies, 2020 activity linked by Group-IB)
targeting.notes: Of 30+ compromised organizations, 24 were in Russia [S3]. Sector list comes from press coverage of the 2019 PT report [S3]; the 2020 government targeting comes from Group-IB via press coverage [S4].

capabilities.summary: Lateral movement and persistence through Windows Task Scheduler task creation [S2]. Use of the ASPXSpy2014 web shell [S3]. Group-IB associates the BlueTraveller/RemShell family with the Webdav-O Trojan, which shares a command set with it and whose x64 variant was used in 2020 attacks; Webdav-O has been seen since at least 2018 [S4].

sources.title: Chinese cyberspies attack Russian government structures (news coverage of the PT report)
Experts described hackers from China who for years attacked Russian companies and government bodies (coverage of the PT report)
Russian federal agencies were attacked with Chinese Webdav-O virus (reporting Group-IB research)

provenance.importedSummary: TaskMasters is a state-sponsored Chinese APT that has been active since at least 2010, primarily targeting industrial, energy, and government sectors in Russia and the CIS. The group has been linked to the Webdav-O Trojan, which employs techniques to bypass network defenses by connecting to legitimate services. Investigations suggest that TaskMasters may have been involved in attacks against Russian federal executive authorities in 2020, potentially alongside another Chinese group, TA428. Additionally, the group has been associated with the BackDoor.RemShell.24 malware, indicating a diverse toolkit in their operations.
